opening.argument: The opportunity is promoted as an unusually easy way to make $36 or more per hour by watching videos and playing games, while being presented as broadly accessible without skill, money, or a credit card. That framing rests on an extrapolation from a stated 15-minute reward: “which means you can make 36 dollars an hour actually just playing video games and testing these video games out and giving valuable feedback to the developers.” Access is not unconditional. Viewers are told that “after this first time you'll be able to get a paid playtest,” and must install a game, record it, and upload the recording. Registration also requests personal information including email, name, devices, country, gender, and birthdate. The qualification requirement and requested data show that the repeated hourly-income claim overstates the observable availability of the opportunity.
